title: White Sox surge past Guardians 4-3 to take 2-0 lead in ALDS and move within 1 win of ALCS
description: The Chicago White Sox defeat the Cleveland Guardians to take a 2-0 series lead in the ALDS.
fullText:
CLEVELAND — The White Sox are returning to Chicago one win from advancing to the American League Championship Series for the first time in 21 years.

Braden Montgomery lined a two-run double down the right-field line in the sixth inning for the go-ahead runs and Sean Burke allowed one hit in 5 1/3 innings of impressive relief as the White Sox rallied past the Cleveland Guardians 4-3 on Monday to take a 2-0 lead in their AL Division Series.

Game 3 is Wednesday afternoon at Guaranteed Rate Field, where the White Sox have two chances to do something they haven't done since 1906 — clinch a postseason series at home.

"They've been waiting 120 years, so maybe we can do it this year," said Grant Taylor, who worked 1 1/3 innings and allowed one hit as he got his second straight save. "I think it's going to be unbelievable. Those fans deserve it. They've been with us for three years of 100 losses and they've been with us a good bit this year giving us a lot of support as we've gone through this. So being able to give them a postseason game is going to be pretty special."

The surprising White Sox improved to 4-0 in these playoffs — all on the road — and are one win from reaching the ALCS for the first time since winning the World Series in 2005. Chicago became the first team to reach the postseason after three straight 100-loss seasons, including a post-1900 record 121 defeats in 2024.

"Our club has been confident the entire year, regardless of the previous result," manager Will Venable said. "They come in ready to play and turn the page. Now, we're really excited to get playoff baseball to our fans."

Munetaka Murakami hit an RBI single in the fourth to get Chicago within 2-1. Chase Meidroth added an RBI single to extend the lead to 4-2.

Jo Adell hit an RBI triple in the eighth and Chase DeLauter had two hits for the Guardians.

Gavin Williams struck out 11, tied for second-most by a Cleveland pitcher in a postseason game. But the offense failed to produce for the second straight game.

"We have had two-game stretches like this all year and we come right back. I've got a lot of faith in this offense. I have a lot of faith in this team," Cleveland manager Stephen Vogt said. "We've got our work cut out for us. Like I said, this team plays its best with its back against the wall."

The White Sox went ahead with a three-run sixth.

Miguel Vargas led off with a base hit to chase Williams and advanced to second on a groundout. Randal Grichuk drew a walk before a wild pitch by losing pitcher Erik Sabrowski with Tommy Pham at the plate advanced the runners to second and third. Pham flied out to shallow left before Montgomery jumped on a first-pitch fastball to drive in the go-ahead runs.

Montgomery celebrated at second base before scoring on Meidroth's single to right.

"I was just ready for something to attack, and I was ready for his hardest stuff. I gave myself my best chance to succeed," Montgomery said. "I can't even describe how it felt. It's exhilarating. I was just taking it all in."

Burke came on with one out in the third. After Travis Bazzana walked with one out in the fourth, the right-hander retired 13 straight batters until DeLauter got a base hit to end Burke's night.

Burke struck out six and threw 83 pitches, including 53 strikes, to earn the win.

"I was able to settle in and find my groove," Burke said. "I've had openers before, but not in this situation, so I talked with a lot of guys. It's just normal baseball when you get into that game."

Taylor entered and allowed an RBI triple to Adell before Nathaniel Lowe flied out to end the eighth.

After getting shut out Saturday, the Guardians struck quickly with a pair of runs in the first.

Steven Kwan led off with a single and José Ramírez walked before Chase DeLauter's grounder off opener Anthony Kay moved the runners to second and third. Sean Newcomb came on and intentionally walked Adell to load the bases. Lowe hit a high chopper to drive in Kwan, but Newcomb threw it wide of the bag at first, allowing Ramírez to score on the error.

It marked the first time in four games this postseason the White Sox were behind.

Kay faced three batters and threw 17 pitches, including eight strikes.

Williams didn't allow a hit until Kyle Teel led off the fourth with a single.

The right-hander allowed two runs and four hits in five-plus innings. He had eight strikeouts in the first three innings and became the first Cleveland pitcher to strike out five straight in a postseason game.

title: LIV Golf, BC Partners file restructuring support agreement in bankruptcy case
description: Late Monday, the long-awaited restructuring support agreement between LIV Golf and BC Partners was filed in the league’s Chapter 11 bankruptcy case.
fullText:
Late Monday, the long-awaited restructuring support agreement between LIV Golf and BC Partners was filed in the league's Chapter 11 bankruptcy case.

The agreement features a $300 million investment by BC into LIV Golf 2.0, which league CEO Scott O'Neil said would feature a scaled-back schedule and a more "disciplined" approach. The RSA also extends the deadline for current LIV Golf players to commit to the restructured league to Oct. 25.

According to LIV Golf's term sheet with BC Partners, which was a part of Monday's filing, players would receive equity in the restructured league as well as signing bonuses and "certain NIL [name, image and likeness] rights." According to the term sheet, "go-forward player ownership will equal 52.5 percent" of LIV Golf 2.0. That would leave 45 percent equity to BC Partners and any minority investors and 2.5 percent equity to management.

"We believe deeply in the future of this league and in the opportunity to build something distinctive alongside our players," O'Neil said in a statement. "We're delivering on our major milestones, and while there is still work ahead, today marks meaningful progress toward a player-owned, team-focused, truly global league that complements the wider game and creates new opportunities for players, fans, partners, and the next generation of golfers."

In August at LIV Golf's season finale, O'Neil referenced the need for a "critical mass" of current players to sign on to version 2.0 but didn't give specifics. While generally he was likely referencing a mixture of stars, like Bryson DeChambeau who has been supportive of the league's next chapter, and lesser-known players, there is also legal element to that number.

According to bankruptcy law, for Chapter 11 restructuring to occur at least two-thirds of the voting creditors from at least 50 percent of the total claims must approve of the restructuring plan. In the case of LIV Golf, the players who are still owed money under existing deals would likely be moved to their own class of creditors, apart from the various vendors who are also a part of the bankruptcy.

Amid LIV bankruptcy case, Sergio Garcia files to terminate contract with league

Sergio Garcia is seeking an exit from his contract with LIV Golf amid the league's Chapter 11 bankruptcy case in New Jersey.

It remains to be seen which players will remain with LIV Golf. Last week, Sergio Garcia submitted a six-page filing in the bankruptcy case asking for clarity regarding the Spaniard's agreement with LIV Golf. "Termination of the agreement is consistent with [LIV Golf's] statement that the agreement is 'not part of [LIV Golf's] go forward business plan' and, accordingly, should not be objectionable to [LIV Golf]," the filing read.

LIV Golf would also have to present a business plan that was considered feasible for the bankruptcy to be approved.

A second-day hearing is scheduled for Wednesday in the New Jersey bankruptcy court but that, according to various sources, will largely be procedural.

If approved by the court at a hearing scheduled for Oct. 14, the RSA will allow LIV Golf to start engaging with key partners — players, sponsors, media partners — regarding a potential go-forward relationship with LIV Golf 2.0. The league could also start preparing for 2027, which O'Neil said would feature 10 events with five tournaments in the United States and five international team events.

title: Red Sox's Craig Breslow Responds to Ben Rice and Cam Schlittler Criticism
description: The Red Sox did what they had to do for the two Yankees' stars.
fullText:
Red Sox's Craig Breslow Responds to Ben Rice and Cam Schlittler Criticism originally appeared on NESN. 

The Boston Red Sox have been impacted by two guys from their backyard, so to say, who are now with the New York Yankees in Cam Schlittler and Ben Rice.

Arguably the best pitcher in all of Major League Baseball, Schlittler played his college days at Northeastern.

Rice, one of the better offensive players in baseball over the past six months, is a New England guy as well. Ultimately, both players would look great in a Red Sox uniform and do a lot for the organization, but there's more to it than the Red Sox missing out on two guys who happened to grow up close to Fenway Park.

At the end of the day, the Red Sox and other teams in Major League Baseball didn't do what was needed to land both of them, and as a result, they're worse off.

The Yankees are the one team out of 29 others that did the right thing in this regard, but similar to every other team in baseball, New York has certainly missed on a lot of other players as well.

According to the latest report, the Red Sox scouted Rice and Schlittler during the draft process, but Craig Breslow responded on Monday morning in a perfect way, perhaps quieting some of the noise from frustrated fans.

"Ray Fagnant, who scouts New England for the Red Sox, recommended both players, but the team passed," the Boston Globe reported.

"I can't speak specifically about Schlittler or Rice. I wasn't here during their drafts. I think there are probably 28 other teams who are saying the exact same thing and what is most important is that we're taking steps to understand how do players like slip through the draft, slip past us, and make sure that when the next player with that ability, is in our backyard, we're taking every opportunity to make sure that they end up in a Red Sox uniform," Breslow said.

While the idea of having Schlittler and Rice in Boston is the right one, it's important to look at context here.

Neither of these guys were marquee prospects, big-time high school recruits, or even great players at every stage of their college careers.

The Red Sox weren't working with some Buster Posey, Stephen Strasburg, or Bryce Harper-caliber player in their backyard. If they were, another team would have selected them before them anyway.

It's easy to look back on what could have been, but truthfully, the same can be said for every team in Major League Baseball, especially the Yankees, who haven't made all the right decisions in their scouting department as well.

title: Rashid Shaheed sees role as tailback
description: Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Rashid Shaheed had two carries for 33 yards, including a 28-yard touchdown in Week 4
fullText:
Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Rashid Shaheed, who also returns kicks, added another title in Week 4 against the Los Angeles Chargers -- tailback. He had two carries for 33 yards, including a 28-yard touchdown. Shaheed was seeing carries with the team light at running back due to rookie RB Jadarian Price on the reserve/injured list, and RB Zach Charbonnet (knee) not quite ready to return from a torn ACL.

"We've had that in all [training] camp," coach Mike Macdonald said Monday, Oct. 5. "This isn't a quote from [offensive coordinator Brian] Fleury, but felt like it was appropriate because of [Price] going down, he gave us some speed. That was cool."

Why it Matters: Shaheed's flirtation as the new Ty Montgomery may be short-lived, as they signed veteran Joe Mixon to the practice squad, while Robert Henry Jr. was also signed from Washington's practice squad. As such, Shaheed is best deployed only in the deepest of fantasy leagues and as an option in specialty leagues which reward individual return yardage.

title: Jake Oettinger posts a shutout as the Stars beat the Sharks 5-0
description: — Jake Oettinger stopped 14 shots and earned his 17th career shutout as the Dallas Stars beat the San Jose Sharks 5-0 on Monday night for their first victory of the season.The Sharks were without star center Macklin Celebrini, who was scratched a few minutes before the start of the game due to a lower-body injury.
fullText:
DALLAS (AP) — Jake Oettinger stopped 14 shots and earned his 17th career shutout as the Dallas Stars beat the San Jose Sharks 5-0 on Monday night for their first victory of the season.

The Sharks were without star center Macklin Celebrini, who was scratched a few minutes before the start of the game due to a lower-body injury.

Jamie Benn had a goal and an assist, and Miro Heiskanen, Joel Kiviranta, Jason Robertson and Mikko Rantanen also scored for Dallas.

Heiskanen's goal on a backhand shot with 1:09 left in the first period proved to be the winner.

Yaroslav Askarov had 21 saves for the Sharks.

Celebrini, who was recently named San Jose's captain, took part in warmups but left the ice earlier than usual.

Former Stars forward Ty Dellandrea made his season debut in place of Celebrini, the 20-year-old face of the franchise who assisted on Igor Chernyshov's overtime goal Saturday that made San Jose 2-0.

Celebrini over the summer signed a five-year, $94 million extension.

TAMPA, Fla. (AP) — Pontus Holmberg and Ilya Mikheyev each had a goal and assist, Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 13 shots to move into a tie for 20th place on the NHL career wins list, and Tampa Bay beat Philadelphia.

Vasilevskiy's 372nd victory moved him into a tie with Andy Moog. Vasilevskiy needs two more wins to tie John Vanbiesbrouck for 19th place.

Brayden Point and Brandon Hagel also scored for the Lightning, who have won two games since an opening-night loss to the New York Rangers.

Tyson Foerster scored for Philadelphia and Dan Vladar finished with 32 saves.

The Flyers are winless (0-2-2) through four games to start the season for the first time since 2013-14. Philadelphia has been held to two or fewer goals in all four games.

Point scored his first goal of the season with a deflection off a wrist shot from John Carlson at 16:05 of the first period. Holmberg scored 17 seconds into the second period off the rush for a 2-0 lead.

Foerster wheeled a shot from the top of the left circle that hit Tampa Bay defenseman Charle-Edouard D'Astous in front of the net to bring Philadelphia with one at 7:22.

Mikheyev made it 3-1 with a wraparound with three minutes to play. Hagel added an empty-netter.

Nikita Kucherov picked up two assists and now has 1,128 career points to move past Mike Bossy and Joe Nieuwendyk for 67th place.

BOSTON (AP) — Tim Stutzle had two goals and an assist and goalies Linus Ullmark and Samuel Ersson combined to stop 18 of 19 shots as Ottawa defeated Boston.

Stutzle's multi-point game moved him into sole possession of sixth place for most points in Ottawa history with 413.

Ullmark started in goal for Ottawa, but wasn't on the ice at the start of the third period. The onetime Bruin netminder, who stopped all 10 shots he faced in the first two periods, was on the bench five minutes into the final period. Ersson made eight saves in the final period for the Senators.

Ottawa's Michael Amadio had a goal and assist, and Drake Batherson also scored.

Boston rookie James Hagan spoiled Ottawa's shutout bid with a goal in the third period. Jeremy Swayman made 20 saves for the Bruins, who have lost two straight after opening the season with two wins.

Boston was outshot 24-19 and failed to score on four power plays.

PITTSBURGH (AP) — Alex Iafallo had a goal and an assist, Clay Stevenson made 29 saves, and Winnipeg beat Pittsburgh.

Pittsburgh's Declan Carlile scored 8:53 into the third period to tie the game at 2-2, but Cole Perfetti scored the winner on a wrist shot just nine seconds later, assisted by Josh Morrissey, to put the Jets ahead to stay.

Adam Lowry also scored for the Jets, who have won two in a row after losing their season opener.

Benjamin Kindel also scored for the Penguins and Carlile added an assist. Sergei Murashov made 30 saves for the Penguins.

The Jets outhit the Penguins by 12, 23 to 11.

title: Guardians in hole after Game 2 loss in ALDS
description: Cleveland fell behind 2-0 to the White Sox in the American League Divisional Series after a 4-3 loss on Monday night.
fullText:
CLEVELAND (WKBN) - The Cleveland Guardians fell behind 2-0 to the Chicago White Sox in the American League Divisional Series after a 4-3 loss on Monday night.

Watch the video above for postgame reaction form Progressive Field!

Guardians starter Gavin Williams struck out 11 batters across 5 innings, becoming the first Cleveland pitcher to reach double-digit strikeouts since Bartolo Colon in 2001.

But the White Sox got to the Guardians bullpen during a three-run sixth inning to give them the lead for good. Jo Adell's RBI triple in the ninth inning wasn't enough to spark a Cleveland comeback.

"Backs against the wall, this is where this team thrives. I mean, you don't want to be in this position. I'm not going to sugarcoat it -- we've backed ourselves into a corner. We know that," Guardians manager Stephen Vogt said. "But if there's anything I know about this group of guys, it's that we love challenges like this, and we're going to embrace it. We're not going to sulk, we're not going to feel sorry for ourselves. We're going to come ready to play on Wednesday, and we know what's ahead of us. We got to go win three in a row, but that starts with one at a time on Wednesday."

The Guardians take on the White Sox in Chicago for Game 3 on Wednesday, Oct. 7, on the brink of elimination.

On Monday night, the Minnesota Timberwolves began their preseason journey with a contest against the Milwaukee Bucks on the road. This was LaMelo Ball's first time to suit up for the Timberwolves in an official setting, and they need all the reps they can get to learn each other's tendencies as they seek to find a breakthrough in the loaded Western Conference.

Ball is going to be the lead ballhandler and playmaker for the Timberwolves, and he is expected to take Minnesota's offense that boasts weapons such as Anthony Edwards and Jaden McDaniels to the next level. But perhaps having Ball around would bring the best out of Rudy Gobert as well.

Out of all the point guards Gobert has played with, Ball is arguably the pest passer he's ever had the privilege of teaming up with. And the two are working hard on their chemistry, as the threat of Ball's scoring paired with Gobert's lob threat should open up a ton of space for the Timberwolves offense.

Gobert is not the best offensive player in the world, and having Ball around to spoon-feed him looks would make his life on that end of the floor that much easier. On the other hand, Gobert is the best defensive player Ball has ever played with, and the 25-year-old guard will have to elevate his level of play on defense to keep up with the Timberwolves.

The Timberwolves did gut their depth in the frontcourt, but this is a sign of trust in Gobert that he can handle the paint-anchoring duties all while the team around him plays some freewheeling basketball.

It will be interesting to see how Gobert acclimates to a much faster style of basketball, as he will be playing with road-runners all around him. And the early previews are at least showing that the four-time Defensive Player of the Year is more than up to the task.

title: New Orleans Pelicans With Most To Gain From Strong Preseason
description: The New Orleans Pelicans kick off their preseason on Tuesday night. Here are the players with the most to gain from a strong batch of games.
fullText:
The New Orleans Pelicans kick off their preseason on Tuesday night against the Oklahoma City Thunder, allowing a look at what this squad is going to look like this season under new coach Jamahl Mosley and his staff.

While most of the excitement will be from how the starters look together and what this defense looks like, there are also a couple of people who need to use this opportunity to make an impact.

Here are the Pelicans who have the most to gain from a strong batch of games before the regular season begins:

Poole is someone who could help transform this team. He is an NBA champion who scored 18.5 points per game on that team. New Orleans hasn't gotten that Golden State Warriors version of him, though.

The 27-year-old was clearly not a fit for whatever the Pelicans had going on, when combined with him battling injuries, it was an ugly year that saw him out of the rotation at times. He posted 13.4 points, 2.0 rebounds and 3.1 assists per night on 37.2/33.3/86.0 shooting splits.

Poole has a chance to start over with this new staff and remind people of what he can do. He'll need to do that to in order to win minutes back with Dejounte Murray and Jeremiah Fears both firmly ahead of him at that guard spot.

Johnson is likely entering a contract year with a looming $5 million option for next year that the team would have to accept before the end of the month. Given what happened with Jordan Hawkins, it would be shocking to see them accept it.

That means that the former first-round pick is going to need to make the most of whatever minutes he gets this year, starting with the preseason.

He needs to show that he can consistently hit threes. Right now, he's shooting 24.5% for his career, but he expects far better from himself. Along with that, this staff is going to be looking for defensive effort.

These three are being lumped in together, because they are currently the odd men out on the roster. Trendon Watford's contract doesn't gain it's next guarantee until Opening Day, but he is certainly a favorite to end up making the team. That puts the onus on the others to stand out and show why they should be the choice. They could also show off for their next teams, as well. Like with Johnson, they can't afford to waste any minutes.

fullText:
ARKADELPHIA, Ark. (KLRT) - For the first time since 2021, Henderson State football is 5-0.

The Reddies have put together a perfect start to the season, and head coach Greg Holsworth says the team's hard work throughout the offseason is paying off.

"Feels really good. I can't be better than 5-0 after five games," Holsworth said. "We've been close around here for a long time and all the work these guys put in in the spring, the summer and just being on the sideline being like, let's go, let's go get this thing guys."

Henderson State's latest win was its toughest test yet.

The Reddies held off a gritty Southwestern Oklahoma State team, 38-33, after trailing for the first time entering the fourth quarter this season.

HSU rallied in the final quarter, outscoring the Bulldogs 14-7. Former Bryant quarterback and Razorback baseball player Austin Ledbetter played a key role in helping the Reddies complete the comeback.

Holsworth said he was proud of the way his team responded when the momentum shifted.

"Really, really proud of them," Holsworth said. "At one point they had all the momentum and we just stayed in the fight. Made some big plays on offense, big plays on defense. And just kept battling and kept battling and eventually took that thing over and got the win."

The 5-0 start has also pushed Henderson State into the national rankings.

The Reddies are No. 17 in the latest Division II AFCA Coaches Poll and are one of 15 unbeaten Division II teams remaining in the country.

But despite the strong start, Holsworth knows his team still has plenty to improve on.

"Focus on the little details. We got a lot to improve on, okay? And in this game showed it," Holsworth said. "Short term negatives turned into long term positives. We messed some stuff up, but you can fix it and get better down the road."

Henderson State will look to make it six straight wins Saturday when the Reddies travel to face Northwestern Oklahoma State.

The Reddies are off to their best start in five years, but they know the bigger goals are still ahead.

fullText:
CLEVELAND (AP) — The Cleveland Guardians have picked a bad time for their offense to go cold again.

Manager Stephen Vogt's squad had one of the worst offenses in the American League before turning it on after the Aug. 3 trade deadline en route to winning its third straight AL Central title.

The offensive surge hasn't carried into the postseason.

Cleveland had only four hits in Monday's 4-3 loss to the Chicago White Sox in Game 2 of their AL Division Series. The Guardians managed just three hits in Saturday's 3-0 loss.

The Guardians had a .231 batting average before the trade deadline, second-worst in the American League. But from Aug. 3 until the end of the regular season, they batted .255, which ranked third.

They don't have much time to get things back on track, with Game 3 on Wednesday in Chicago as Cleveland tries to avoid getting swept in a Division Series for the first time since 2018 against Houston.

"I think we've done a really good job of flushing games. Have the day off tomorrow, make sure we have some good focus, but obviously, yeah, not how you wanted to finish Game 2," outfielder Steven Kwan said.

It is only the fourth time since Division Series started in 1995 that a team has had seven or fewer hits over the first two games. The others were the 2008 Milwaukee Brewers, 2010 Cincinnati Reds (who were no-hit by Philadelphia in Game 1) and 2018 Cleveland Indians.

Cleveland's leadoff hitter has reached base only twice in the two games and the team is 0 for 8 with runners in scoring position.

The White Sox going with bullpen games in the first two games of the series has also put Cleveland hitters off balance.

"They made great pitches and we battled and we haven't given any at-bats away. And I think the name of the game is, `Who Lands a Pitch?' And when they made those mistakes, we just weren't able to capitalize maybe in the way we wanted to, but that's part of the game," outfielder Jo Adell said.

Adell gave Cleveland some fleeting hope in the eighth with an RBI triple to get the Guardians within one run. But then Nathaniel Lowe flied out to end the inning.

"We put good swings up (in the late innings) and I think that's what we're capable of," Adell said. "We had a lot of those balls that, mine included, I for sure though it was out and it's one of those days where it didn't travel that way and that's the way the game is. But we're convicted in our approach and our at-bats and we have a bunch of really good players in here, so we're going to continue to fight."

Cleveland's struggles on offense wasted a strong start from Gavin Williams, whose 11 strikeouts were tied for second-most in team history in a postseason game.

The right-hander — who led the AL in strikeouts this season — struck out eight in the first three innings and became the first pitcher in franchise history to whiff five straight in a postseason game. He also had 16 pitches over 100 mph, the fourth-most by an AL pitcher in a playoff game since tracking started in 2008.

His 0-2 fastball to Munetaka Murakami in the fourth inning registered 101.2 mph, which was the hardest pitch of his career.

"I feel like I've been doing it all year. It just wasn't today. I know I've hit 101 a couple times this year, but could be the juices, too," Williams said. "I don't think I was too worried about the strikeouts. Just trying to put the team in a good position to win."

Williams — who allowed two runs and four hits — came out in the sixth after allowing a leadoff single to Miguel Vargas. The White Sox scored three times that inning off Erik Sabrowski and Hunter Gaddis to take the lead.

"We couldn't have asked any more from Gavin other than maybe a few more pitches. He did his job and then some. That is a big-time performance by a big-time pitcher," Vogt said.

title: ‘What Are You Talking About?,’ ‘Welcome to Big-Time Sports!’ — Ex-Indiana Coach Tells Kelsey Mitchell to ‘Grow Up’ Amid Caitlin Clark Controversy
description: Indiana Fever star Kelsey Mitchell opened up about the criticism she receives from fans just by playing next to Caitlin Clark. Mitchell admitted this has created difficulties for her, which could influence what she plans to do this offseason.
fullText:
Indiana Fever star Kelsey Mitchell opened up about the criticism she receives from fans just by playing next to Caitlin Clark. Mitchell admitted this has created difficulties for her, which could influence what she plans to do this offseason.

Sportscaster Dan Dakich took exception to Mitchell's comments and did not mince words in calling her out.

Indiana has been at the center of the spotlight over the past few years, largely due to Clark's arrival in 2024.

However, she hasn't just brought increased popularity with her. The 24-year-old has invited scrutiny toward her teammates, which has weighed heavily on Mitchell.

Following the Fever's first-round exit at the hands of the Las Vegas Aces, Mitchell opened up about how fans have treated her.

The 2018 No. 2 pick claimed that people do not understand how difficult it is to be a professional athlete. She went on to frame the scrutiny and criticism she is subjected to as stemming from being Clark's teammate.

"Playing with CC and having the eyes that she got, we get a lot of flak just for being on her team," Mitchell said. "… I just think that people got to give us grace. I think this organization is unbelievable, man, but I think that when it comes to really trying to be yourself, it hasn't always been easy."

Dakich, a former interim coach of the Indiana Hoosiers, responded to Mitchell's comments on "Don't @ Me" on Monday.

"Let's understand something, Kelsey. Sports fans have disliked their own teams ten minutes into the sports being invented," Dakich said.

He then went on to cite various instances of fans going after the players of the teams they support over on-court mistakes.

"Ask an NBA player who misses shot after shot in Game 6, Game 7. I mean, what are you talking about?" Dakich continued. "You want everybody to wake up and go, 'Oh my god, it's a fever fan.' Welcome to big-time sports.

"I mean, you all want big-time sports, as Sophie Cunningham said. And now you [expletive], whine, and moan, and you act coy and cute and all that little [expletive] that you're doing right there because you're getting scrutiny? … Welcome to big-time sports, little girl. Now grow up, be a woman, be an adult."

Mitchell has played nine years in the WNBA, all with the Fever. Prior to Clark's arrival, she was the offensive engine that ran the team.

In the six years before Clark was drafted, she averaged 16.4 points and 3.0 assists per game and was named an All-Star in 2023. However, the team constantly struggled, winning fewer than 10 games in four of those six seasons.

Clark's arrival in 2024 rejuvenated the team. She helped them reach 20 wins for the first time since 2015 in her maiden season. Additionally, that year marked the end of the franchise's seven-year postseason drought.

MORE: 'Most Important Offseason' — ESPN Legend Urges Fever to Bolster Roster Around Caitlin Clark

Mitchell's game also seemed to get elevated by playing alongside Clark. Since 2024, her scoring has increased yearly, and she has earned three straight All-Star nods. This season, she put up a career-high 24.7 points per game.

The backcourt duo of Mitchell and Clark is considered one of the best superstar pairings in the WNBA. However, it could soon be coming to an end.

The four-time All-Star enters the offseason as an unrestricted free agent. Several teams are sure to show interest, especially with Mitchell coming off a career year.

After her telling comments during her season-ending press conference, some believe she will test free agency. If she chooses to sign elsewhere, one of the league's best one-two combos would be abruptly separated before reaching the level of success many expected.

title: Four observations as Yankees now face elimination with ALDS Game 2 loss
description: The Yankees are one loss from elimination. Four key observations and takeaways from their ALDS Game 2 loss to the Rays.
fullText:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. - This was the Rays' way, on full display in a pivotal Game 2.

Put the ball in play, use speed and daring on the bases and force the defense - in this case a skittish group of Yankees infielders - to make plays, or mistakes.

Cam Schlittler wasn't at his best Monday night, but the Yankees threatened a franchise postseason record for errors in one game at Tropicana Field, where the Rays own a huge house advantage.

Under the dome and on the spongy artificial surface, the Yankees' 5-2 loss pushed them to the brink elimination as this best-of-five AL Division Series shifts to the Bronx on Wednesday night.

Here are our takeaways from a lost Game 2:

This is where it all unraveled, with a four-run fifth inning that broke open a 1-1 game.

Jonathan Aranda (single) and Junior Caminero (double) opened at second and third. From there, two misplays by rookie shortstop George Lombard Jr. led to two runs.

Schlittler was gone after 76 stressful pitches (7 hits, 1 walk, just 2 strikeouts), leading to Richie Palacios' sharp, two-run single off a full-count pitch by Brent Headrick.

Just before that two-out hit made it 5-1, Lombard - with a runner crossing in front of him as he fielded Jonny DeLuca's grounder - rushed a wide throw to first for an error.

The first two runs off Schlittler were the product of soft contact, but highlighted the Rays' ability to pressure a defense with their speed and ability to put the ball in play - even against a pitcher with three different fastballs at high octane who'll be a shoe-in Cy Young Award winner next month.

Both came with the Yanks' infield in.

Liam Hicks' soft bouncer toward second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. took away his play at the plate, settling for the out at first.

Next up, Chandler Simpson, possibly the fastest runner in game, sent a weak grounder to Lombard, who whiffed on a rushed backhanded attempt, looking for a play at the plate.

Originally scored an error, it went as an infield hit and the Rays had a 3-1 lead.

And it could've been even worse.

Tampa Bay led 1-0 after the first, an inning where the Yanks' committed three errors - including a throwing error by second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. that scored the unearned run.

Chisholm's second errant toss cost the Yanks a synch inning-ending double play, but Schlittler picked up his teammates in that 19-pitch frame.

It started with a leadoff error by third baseman Ryan McMahon on Yandy Diaz's grounder and included a would-be third strike erased by Austin Wells' catcher's interference on Liam Hicks.

The Yanks' inability to take care of the ball has been a fundamental issue at times, and it has cost them in postseason, most notably in the decisive World Series Game 5 vs. the Dodgers.

Chisholm's error was a reckless play; he had no shot at doubling up Caminero, who was well across first base as the second baseman's off-balance throw went wild.

Ben Rice's two-homer night gave him four in four postseason games this year.

Leading off the fourth inning against Peralta, the lefty-hitting Rice's game-tying solo home was the Yanks first hit Monday, after being one-hit in Game 1 by Drew Rasmussen and Bryan Baker.

Rice's love affair with the Trop continued with a solo shot in the eighth off lefty Ian Seymour, making Rice a .448 hitter (13-for-29) this year - including postseason - under St. Pete's outdated dome, with seven home runs and 12 RBI.

Of course, we were bound to have some catwalk chaos here too, when Spencer Jones' towering fly to start the second inning struck the B-ring (in play).

But right fielder Victor Mesa Jr. made the catch - which otherwise would've likely been a fly out to center.

Before the game, Yanks manager Aaron Boone said he though about some alteration to his lineup.

But he ultimately felt convicted in running back the same order that was no-hit by Drew Rasmussen into the eighth inning of Game 1.

Once change he could've made was for McMahon, who entered 1-for-14 vs. starter Freddy Peralta, who lasted 4.2 innings.

Yet to see a 2026 postseason at-bat entering Monday, Jose Caballero (0-for-2 career vs. Peralta) was one possible choice.

Anthony Volpe (2-for-4, double, HR career vs. Peralta) was another, but that small sample size, plus Boone's reluctance to play him at third base at the Trop was a factor.

McMahon (0-for-1) did draw a full-count walk that ended Peralta's night in the fifth inning.

title: Did the Tigers Fail With Tarik Skubal?
description: Wasted postseason dominance and a painful blockbuster trade define the Tarik Skubal era. Explore whether Detroit squandered a generational ace or played their hand perfectly for the future.
fullText:
The question is simple: Did the Detroit Tigers fail while Tarik Skubal donned the Old English D?

The answer, though, may not be as simple as you may think.

I'm not here to convince you whether they did or didn't, much like I would never try to convince you who the Asscrack Bandit is.

But I will say my side of the story.

Before I dive into it, I want to make one thing clear: The Tigers did the right thing by trading Skubal.

It needed to happen. The deal was never going to get done, and even with distant rumors of potentially reuniting Skubal and Detroit, the deal was never going to happen.

Detroit got what it could, pulled the trigger early, and that still doesn't bother me. The Dodgers were going to move on and leave us with less somewhere else.

Or at least that's what I'm telling myself.

As much hate as Scott Harris receives, trading Skubal was the correct decision, as painful as it was.

However, the Tigers did have Skubal in his prime, along with two teams that were good enough to make some noise.

Detroit made the postseason in consecutive seasons, with Skubal playing a massive role in both.

The first was the most miraculous run of the two in 2024.

Detroit legitimately leaned on the back of Skubal every five days while trying to piece together a Frankenstein's monster of a pitching staff for the other four.

The Tigers went from having a 0.2% chance of making the playoffs to actually making the playoffs.

Detroit then met the skipper's old team, the Houston Astros, where A.J. Hinch had been fired following the cheating scandal that rocked the baseball world.

Hinch and the Tigers took care of business in the Wild Card round.

The Tigers' magical season came crashing to a halt against their division rival in the ALDS. Detroit folded under the pressure, but it was still a moral victory.

A team that wasn't projected to make the playoffs had done the impossible and made a name for itself.

The following year, the Tigers came out of the gate on a warpath.

Then they quickly folded late in the season, surrendering the division lead to Cleveland.

And who did they meet in the Wild Card round?

This time, Detroit was finally able to slay the beast.

From there, Detroit went on to play Seattle in the ALDS, where Skubal struck out 22 batters across two starts and finished with a 2.08 ERA.

Detroit struggled offensively and ultimately fell in extra innings in the series-deciding game.

The offseason proved Detroit had no realistic chance of re-signing Skubal, so the Tigers spent elsewhere, bringing in Framber Valdez and Justin Verlander.

Detroit had one year with Skubal and a team built to win a championship.

I would count 2024 as a championship-caliber opportunity, too, but for what it was: a miraculous season that went as far as it probably ever could have.

But in 2025, at the trade deadline, the Tigers knew that in just one year they would not be retaining the best pitcher in baseball.

The fans didn't necessarily look that far ahead yet, but those who did knew it.

And instead of making one final push with the best pitcher in baseball, the Tigers traded for cast-off bullpen arms that ultimately became part of the team's demise, alongside an offense that was never properly addressed.

The Tigers front office does everything it can to avoid the correct questions.

And because of that, yes, I believe the Tigers absolutely failed with Skubal on the roster.

They failed because they had one of the best pitchers in baseball, two legitimate opportunities to make a deep postseason run, and a finite amount of time to build a championship team around him.

The failure was what came before it.

PROVIDENCE, RI (WPRI) — This week's Cardi's Furniture & Mattresses Hometown Sports Hero is Alyssa Parenteau.

The LaSalle Academy All-Stater won Gold in the 1500 meters, Indoors and Outdoors last year, breaking through as a Junior for the Rams. Her success bringing her plenty of college attention, including from the Big East program next door to LaSalle. Providence College proving to be the perfect fit for Parenteau on and off the Track, and she verbally committed to the Friars last week.

"They have a great new Health Science building which they have so much funding in and it was awesome and it fit all my needs academically and then obviously Athletically, I wanted to be at a school and on a team that pushed me," Parenteau said. "And as soon as I was at PC, I felt like I was at home and I was like, I can really strive with this group of girls and these Coaches."

"I know when Alyssa gets there, she's going to do great things because she is probably one of the hardest working, most motivated athletes I've ever coached," said Rams Cross Country Coach Kelly Raso.

Her Dad started her on the Track at age 7, and the drive it takes to succeed, pushing it ahead of Soccer and Basketball.

"I just love the sport, it's not even about success, it's all about the friends I have made through it and everything I've learned," Parenteau said. "So, I just love running and I love pushing myself and I'm very determined."

With her college decision complete, Alyssa can bring all her focus into her Senior Year. Making a run at the State Cross Country Title and repeating her 1,500 Meter Golds are top of her mind, as well as breaking a 5-minute mile. Challenging herself to the maximum over the next three seasons, the best way to prepare for Providence College.

"Definitely, being committed is a big relief now but I also feel like it gives me something to push for, knowing I'm committed to such a great team, I want to fit that standard and show that I am good enough," Parenteau said. "So, I feel like a lot of peace in myself, knowing that I'm just going to work hard everyday and keep my head down."

title: OU football QB John Mateer used Sooners' bye week to 'reset' and silence doubters
description: Following a bye week that served as a much-needed rest, OU football quarterback John Mateer is looking to prove everyone wrong come Saturday against Texas.
fullText:
NORMAN — The bye week was a breath of fresh air for John Mateer.

Oklahoma's quarterback has endured constant criticism after a disappointing start to the season and used the time off last week to recenter, assess what has gone wrong through four weeks and spend time with his teammates, who have reinforced their belief in their leader.

"I had a good break personally," Mateer said after practice Monday. "We had great practices, hung out with some of the guys. Went out to dinner. It was a reset because (during the season), you don't really get time to — you do, but not as much as the offseason."

Mateer knows what's at stake this week.

OU football bowl projections 2026: Where are Sooners entering Texas game?

A year after he put his all into returning for this game — the Red River Rivalry against Texas — 17 days post-surgery, Mateer finds himself up against it again. His confidence was clearly shot after turning the ball over on three consecutive drives in a blowout road loss to Georgia in which his coaches pondered benching him.

He knows he must improve and take care of the ball to give the Sooners any shot against the No. 1-ranked Longhorns on Saturday at the Cotton Bowl in Dallas. Mateer's turnovers have been catastrophic for OU after his interception against Michigan all but sealed a Wolverines win and his two fumbles against Georgia resulted in two Bulldogs touchdowns.

Last season's Texas game when he threw three interceptions is one he still thinks about. Not so much because of what it took to play but about how he played and how he wears that loss.

"We're ready to go," Mateer said. "Everybody, you get to sit back and look at where we're at, and we're ready to go. I'm more excited. It's the game, it is what everybody says it is. It's awesome and I'm honored to play in it, in a rivalry and for this team and for these guys.

"Last year, it was what it was. It's taught me a lot but I'm standing here and ready to play this week."

Here’s #Sooners QB John Mateer on the bye week, Red River Rivalry and where his confidence is at. pic.twitter.com/HVgZIOu7o2

Mateer has stayed off social media so he hasn't heard the constant negativity surrounding his play. But he undeniably feels it.

He has a good support system around him that has helped him through this over the last several weeks. OU certainly has devoted all of its resources to help every player but especially Mateer as he endures this rut.

There have been thoughts that his play might fracture the team or divide one unit against another. That hasn't been the case at all as the Sooners' leaders have rallied around Mateer.

"The fact that I haven't performed is disappointing, but I'm blessed to play ball today and to get better," Mateer said. "It's a kids game that we all take really seriously, and I'm honored to stand here and be this person in this position. But you come out to practice today knowing that it's everything I've ever dreamed of.

"So even when you struggle and you get judged, it's because I've done good in the past to put me (where) something is expected from me — from me and from other people. It's the position I'm in, but I'm learning."

More: Will disgruntled OU football fans air their grievances during Red River Rivalry?

Mateer said this offseason how much it meant to him when general manager Jim Nagy and coach Brent Venables reaffirmed their commitment to him after an up-and-down 2025 season. Venables did it once again last week, announcing Mateer is still OU's starter.

Whether or not anyone else does, it's clear the Sooners still believe Mateer gives them the best chance to win. That could change Saturday.

Following the bye week, Mateer is ready to attack this week of practice and focus on improving as much as he can before Saturday. For someone who needs all the help he can get with getting his confidence back to where it needs to be, the support he's gotten around him means the world.

He has a chance to silence all of the doubters Saturday.

"It helps, it really does," Mateer said. "The tight ends came over Sunday after the game and watched some football. I appreciate that. And the receivers, we're talking ball and just hanging out and they say it. (Defensive ends coach Miguel Chavis), he's been great, and (offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle), (quarterbacks coach John Kuceyeski) and Coach Venables.

" ... He tells me straight up, like, he has my back and he's proud of the work and the toughness, and I appreciate that more than he knows, more than I can say."

title: Oscar De La Hoya doubts Ryan Garcia joins Dana White after current deal expires: Not 'a good fit for him'
description: Oscar De La Hoya weighs in on Ryan Garcia's future and the ongoing war between Dana White and Eddie Hearn.
fullText:
Oscar De La Hoya has picked a side in boxing's civil war between Eddie Hearn and Dana White.

"I am Team Eddie right now, because he's cooking Dana," De La Hoya told Uncrowned's "The Ariel Helwani Show" on Monday.

Hearn and White's continued public exchanges over the UFC CEO's involvement in the Dec. 11 fight between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua have provided plenty of entertainment for the boxing world.

De La Hoya said he hopes to launch his own confrontation with White and TKO's Zuffa Boxing in the near future, with what he describes as the "clap-back of the century," but for now he is happy to watch Hearn take the lead.

"It is the funniest thing I've ever seen," De La Hoya said. "These guys just don't stop. You know Eddie, Eddie's just funny. He's harmless. That's why Eddie and I get along so well now. We had our differences, and he knows exactly what he has to do for his fighters, and he's a promoter.

"I'm just sitting back right here collecting all my information, having a great time listening to these guys bickering back and forth."

De La Hoya's assessment of White was considerably less generous.

Throughout the year, White has repeated the line that boxing fans should judge Zuffa Boxing at the end of 2026 based on its complete "body of work." We are now in October, and it's safe to say that De La Hoya has already reached his conclusion.

"Let's just say if I was a teacher, [they'd] be getting an F," De La Hoya said in his assessment of Zuffa Boxing.

"What has he done? All they do is rent fighters. They don't know how to build champions. They don't know how to build fighters from scratch. It's crazy. It's ridiculous. This sport of boxing, you have to be invested emotionally, and you have to put in your time and get to know the fighters and make it personal.

"Dana doesn't know s*** about fighters. He doesn't want to get to know them. It's all about a number for him. You take a look at TKO and the UFC — it's all about numbers and their shareholders. Boxing is more personal. You have to know the fighters. You have to have some interest in their lives and make sure that they're OK and make sure that they're treated correctly.

"Not send an email firing a fighter. You don't do it like that. That's not the way to do things, not in boxing."

De La Hoya was referring to Zuffa informing former WBC light heavyweight champion Oleksandr Gvozdyk of his release via email in April.

Gvozdyk fought just once with the promotional company, dominating Radivoje Kalajdzic through six rounds and scoring two knockdowns in the process, but ultimately succumbed in a dramatic seventh-round stoppage loss.

Although Gvozdyk was understanding of Zuffa's decision, the cutthroat nature of his release didn't go down well with some boxing fans. Some questioned the move after White said upon his entry into the sport that he aimed to get boxers to stop protecting their zeros and take the best fights — yet, when a former champion lost in a bout he was dominating, he was not given a second chance.

Yet if De La Hoya didn't already dislike White and TKO, he was certainly given a reason to after his alleged exclusion from September's Ryan Garcia vs. Conor Benn fight.

Garcia is De La Hoya's biggest star of a client, but the show — a Ring event co-promoted by Zuffa Boxing and De La Hoya's Golden Boy — was firmly positioned as a TKO and Zuffa product, with De La Hoya missing from the entire promotion and fight night.

"I didn't have my ringside tickets," De La Hoya explained about his absence. " … They gave me tickets, but not where I was contractually obligated to sit down."

"The event turned out excellent for Ryan Garcia," De La Hoya continued. "He had the great knockout, I'm very happy for him, but the fact that they kept me out of it — oooh."

De La Hoya said he plans to discuss his exclusion from the event on a future edition of his social media series "clap-back Thursday." He did, however, claim White was not the man behind it.

"Dana has no say whatsoever," De La Hoya said. "He doesn't have any pull here. Let's just say that I cannot talk about it until the smoke clears. There's some legalities that we have to deal with and all that stuff. I have 'clap-back' for a reason, and that's to tell you the truth. And once my muzzle is off, I can't wait."

Although Garcia was disappointed that De La Hoya wasn't at his fight, De La Hoya said the pair have spoken since, and all is good between them.

Garcia has one fight remaining on his promotional deal with Golden Boy — although sources close to the situation told Uncrowned that Garcia has an additional fight with DAZN left on his contract.

De La Hoya has helped develop Garcia into one of boxing's biggest stars and hopes to continue working with him after their current contract expires. Garcia, however, has said in the past that he doesn't intend to re-sign.

Whether Garcia stays with Golden Boy or not, De La Hoya doubts the WBC welterweight champion will be aligning with White.

"I don't think he'll go with Zuffa," De La Hoya said. "I don't think that's a good fit for him."

The Golden Boy founder said he will meet with Garcia imminently to discuss Garcia's next fight — though De La Hoya already knows who he'd like to see Garcia fight next.

"The guy that I wanted in the first place, Devin Haney," De La Hoya revealed. "Devin Haney and Teofimo [Lopez] are the biggest fights out there for Ryan, and Ryan is at an elite level right now. He's the guy who should be fighting the top guys and the very best.

"What I love about Ryan is that he has something very competitive in him where he wants to fight the very best and he wants to show the world that he is the best. A Teofimo or a Devin Haney is the perfect choice for him."

De La Hoya has clear ideas about what should come next for Garcia. The less certain question is whether he will remain the man promoting Garcia beyond that.

title: Rays beat Yankees 5-2 to take 2-0 ALDS lead
description: (AP) — Richie Palacios hit a two-run single in a four-run fifth inning and the Tampa Bay Rays took advantage of New York’s sloppy defense, beating Cam Schlittler and the Yankees 5-2 on Monday night to take a 2-0 lead in their AL Division Series.The Rays are one victory from reaching the American League Championship Series.
fullText:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. (AP) — Richie Palacios hit a two-run single in a four-run fifth inning and the Tampa Bay Rays took advantage of New York's sloppy defense, beating Cam Schlittler and the Yankees 5-2 on Monday night to take a 2-0 lead in their AL Division Series.

The Rays are one victory from reaching the American League Championship Series. Game 3 in the best-of-five playoff is Wednesday night at Yankee Stadium.

Ben Rice hit a pair of homers for the Yankees, who are on the verge of elimination — which would extend their World Series drought to 17 seasons. They were dominated by Drew Rasmussen in the series opener and have scored just two runs in two games with three-time AL MVP Aaron Judge out of the lineup due to a calf injury.

The small-ball Rays chased Schlittler, the likely AL Cy Young Award winner, in the fifth aided by New York's defensive miscues.

Jonathan Aranda lined a single to start the inning and Junior Caminero ripped a double to right-center. With the infield drawn-in except second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr., who was standing several feet further back on the dirt, Liam Hicks hit a bouncer to second that scored Aranda for a 2-1 lead. Chisholm's only play was at first because he wasn't all the way in like the rest of the infielders.

Chandler Simpson then hit a grounder that shortstop George Lombard Jr. booted, scoring Caminero to make it 3-1. It was initially ruled a hit and then changed to an error and eventually a fielder's choice. Brent Headrick replaced Schlittler and struck out Victor Mesa Jr. After Simpson stole second, Jonny DeLuca reached on a grounder when Lombard's throw to first was wide for New York's fourth error.

Palacios followed with a hard single to center that increased Tampa Bay's lead to 5-1.

That was plenty of support for one of the best bullpens in the majors.

Freddy Peralta allowed one run and three hits in 4 2/3 innings, Cam Booser pitched out of a bases-loaded jam in the fifth and Ian Seymour gave up one run on Rice's solo shot in three innings. Bryan Baker finished with a perfect ninth for his second save in two games.

Schlittler, who was 14-6 with a 1.95 ERA and dominated Boston in the opener of the wild-card round, lasted 4 1/3 innings. He allowed four runs — two earned — and six hits. Schlittler only fanned two.

CLEVELAND (AP) — Braden Montgomery lined a two-run double down the right-field line, Sean Burke allowed one hit in 5 1/3 innings of splendid relief and Chicago beat Cleveland to take a 2-0 lead in their AL Division Series.

The surprising White Sox improved to 4-0 in these playoffs — all on the road — and are one win from advancing to the American League Championship Series for the first time since winning the World Series in 2005. Chicago became the first team to reach the postseason after three straight 100-loss seasons, including a post-1900 record 121 defeats in 2024.

Jo Adell hit an RBI triple in the eighth and Chase DeLauter had two hits for the Guardians.

Starting pitcher Gavin Williams struck out 11, tied for second-most in a Cleveland postseason game. But the offense failed to produce for the second straight game.

Grant Taylor worked 1 1/3 innings and allowed one hit as he got his second straight save.

The best-of-five series shifts to Chicago for Game 3 on Wednesday.

title: Report: Minnesota Twins Sale Back On
description: After previously taking them off the market, the Pohlads are quietly moving towards a sale of the Minnesota Twins.
fullText:
The Pohlad family has owned the Minnesota Twins since 1984, but the relationship between ownership and the fanbase has been strained for much of those 40+ years. So far, we've had four different family members (through multiple generations) take the spot as top Pohlad in charge.

Obviously, Carl Pohlad first purchased the team from Calvin Griffith, who brought the Senators here from Washington, D.C., in 1960 and changed their name from the Senators to the Twins (first season in MN was 1961). Carl then ran the team from 1984-2009, when he handed the organization off to his son, Jim Pohlad, who did the same until November 2022.

That's when the reins were given to Joe Pohlad, Jim's nephew. Joe's time in the big chair is remembered for signing Carlos Correa and running up enough debt ($500M) that they had to sell 20% to minority investors in order to keep it from spinning out of control.

Of course, the Twins started pushing up their debt ceiling long before Joe took charge. Still, he proved ill-equipped for the situation. Thus, three years after he took charge, Joe Pohlad was relieved of his duties as executive chair.

With new investors in tow, Joe's older brother Tom Pohlad was brought in to run the family baseball business. Since his arrival, Tom has been determined to set a different tone than past Pohlads.

Here's the video of my payroll question and Tom Pohlad's response: https://t.co/3yqL7HwaIR pic.twitter.com/wnszAPi46G

— Aaron Gleeman (@AaronGleeman) September 29, 2026

We've heard him talk big about future payroll increases, comments he recently doubled down on, vowing to "meaningfully invest" in the roster this offseason, even noting that a $100 million payroll isn't sufficient in Major League Baseball going forward.

Some of his promises and antics have landed better than others. But trust isn't earned in a day, and nobody is learning that better than this billionaire family.

And let's be real, a large portion of the fanbase doesn't care what any Pohlad has to say these days. They stopped listening a long time ago, and for good reason. Many have even vowed to never watch a Minnesota Twins game again until they have sold the team.

Well, we caught wind of some rumors this weekend that they may want to tune in for. According to Charley Walters (Pioneer Press), the Pohlads are getting serious about selling the team yet again.

Pssst: A sale of the Twins to the New York-based global investment firm Varde Partners, which has an office in Minneapolis and in 2025 became a Twins limited partner to help the franchise out of $500 million in debt, is said to be heating up. Varde Partners reportedly manages $15 billion in assets.

Charley Walters – Pioneer Press

Minnesota Twins fans have gone through this song and dance before, and won't believe they've been relieved of the Pohlad family until it's actually set in legal stone.

It's also worth noting that the current CBA expires December 1, with a lockout widely expected to follow. So everything about baseball's future is up in the air until that gets figured out, including all of these Pohlad promises (and any chance that they sell).

As Walters — a former Minnesota Twins pitcher who's been scooping sports news for the past five decades — notes in his article at the Pioneer Press, Varde Partners came aboard as a limited partner in 2025, taking on equity to help clear the Pohlads' ever-expanding debt at the time.

Now, per Walters, they're looking for a bigger piece of the pie. While the Pohlads initially suggested there were no set triggers for the limited partners to take on further ownership, the family's interest in a sale has never really gone away.

The reality is that Carl Pohlad purchased the MN Twins for $44 million in 1984. Even had they sold for the $1.5 billion valuation they refused to accept the first time around, the family would've netted more than a 3,000% return, with an annualized return of nearly 9%.

Instead, with the changes expected to take place this winter through CBA negotiations, they'll now be seeking a $2 billion valuation, per Walters.

With a new baseball economic model, the Pohlad family, which sought $1.75 billion for the Twins two years ago, could expect in excess of $2 billion going forward.

Charley Walters – Pioneer Press

Last time they were on the open market the family reportedly sought $1.75 billion, though the debt would have brought their net closer to $1.25 billion. It's possible the new outlying factors could push their value well above that.

The Los Angeles Angels ($4B) and San Diego Padres ($3.9B) both sold in 2026 for FAR MORE than what the Minnesota Twins were asking prior to those deals being done.

Ultimately, this offseason could prove pivotal in an adjustment of the Minnesota Twins' overall value. A salary cap being instituted across Major League Baseball would only further accelerate values with spending being capped and revenues continuing to grow. A new television deal being expected in 2028 with ESPN would throw gasoline on growth as well.

Over four decades of ownership, the Pohlad run has included World Series titles in 1987 and 1991 and the opening of Target Field in 2010. Everything in between has been mostly a disaster… or an unstoppable train on the way to that. And going all the way back to Carl, tight pockets have been an ongoing issue.

Did you know Jack Morris and his agent sat down with Carl Pohlad and Andy MacPhail prior to the 1987 season, but were unable to reach a deal? #MNTwinsIt was later determined that owners conspired against free agents during this time period. (Collusion led to Carew's retirement) https://t.co/H1XMYbfUtV

— The Twins Almanac (@TwinsAlmanac) May 20, 2021

For many fans, the Minnesota Twins moving on from the Pohlad family would be welcome news. While what Varde Partners, or anyone else for that matter, would do with the franchise is unknown, new ownership is undoubtedly the preferred result for the majority of this fanbase.

There are a significant number of family members with a stake in the franchise, but it's an asset that doesn't make the family much (if any?) cash until it is sold.

In the meantime, the Pohlads have sold off businesses like Carousel Motor Group, and remain heavily invested in commercial real estate. Not every member of the family has the same ties to baseball, either. So there is lots of motivation to sell, some financial, some personal, and some undoubtedly both.

title: Falcons – Saints Week 4 instant recap: Beatdown in the bayou
description: Atlanta smokes the Saints on their own field, and we’re overjoyed.
fullText:
The Atlanta Falcons came into a pressure-packed primetime rivalry game needing a crisp performance. They put on their ass kicking cleats and got one.

The Falcons led early. They led in the middle of the game. They led late. They were dominant almost wire-to-wire, with a couple of coverage miscues, frustrating penalties, and misses from Michael Penix Jr. the only things slowing them down. They were up 24-7 at halftime and 31-10 at the end of the third quarter, with the absurdly great performance from the ground game and terrific run defense conspiring to deliver a big win for the second straight week.

It is absolutely striking how well they're playing, even if the Packers and Saints are a bit depleted. Tommy Rees had the offense rolling, Michael Penix Jr. hit some big time throws, Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson terrorized the defense, Jahan Dotson joined Kyle Pitts and Drake London in the big play party, and the defense harried Tyler Shough and largely shut down New Orleans' feckless runners. Atlanta has had so many struggles against the Saints over the past two decades that three straight wins against New Orleans and a dominant effort like this one are beyond welcome, and this was simply one of the most lopsided victories in the long history of this rivalry. It was spectacular, wondrous, and one of my favorite watches in recent memory. I hope it was for you, too.

Here's a play-by-play recap of the game you just watched.

The Falcons let the opening kickoff roll through the landing zone and into the end zone, giving them the start at the 20 yard line. Drake London got a quick throw from Michael Penix Jr., stiff-armed a Saint into the dirt, and spun his way to a first down. Austin Hooper got a quick screen and picked up nine yards. On the next play, the handoff went to Bijan Robinson, who got nice blocks from Jake Matthews, Ryan Neuzil, and Matthew Bergeron and went untouched for 59 yards and a touchdown. 7-0 Falcons.

The Saints returned the ball to about the 28 yard line. Tyler Shough's first down throw was behind Chris Olave, who saw the ball knocked down anyways. CJ Henderson was hurt on the play. Under pressure, Shough hit Devaughn Vele for two yards. Shough then tried Bryce Lance way downfield but missed by several yards. CJ Henderson was back, Za'Darius Smith was injured. He thankfully was able to walk off the field on his own power after a scary delay. Zachariah Branch fielded the fair catch, but a holding call on New Orleans backed the Saints up ten more yards. On the re-punt, Branch made a couple guys miss and took it almost the 50 yard line.

Penix hit Branch on the sideline for a quick nine yards. Bijan took the next carry about five yards for a first down. Penix then tried a shot to a diving London, who couldn't grab it. Robinson then took it another four yards on second down. On third down, Penix backpedaled under pressure and missed Dotson down the sideline. There was a delay of game on the next play, as the ball just wasn't snapped in time. The Jake Bailey punt was fair caught inside the 15 yard line.

The Saints got the Falcons for an encroachment and five yards, with the call against Maason Smith. Kendre Miller's carry went for a loss of about a yard, with Sydney Brown flying in. The Saints then got hit with a false start. Shough was nearly brought down for a safety by Zach Harrison, but hit Juwan Johnson working against Henderson for 23 yards. Alvin Kamara then picked up four yards. Shough then hit Kamara for five yards, with Brown flying in to make the tackle. Shough plunged up the middle for a first down. A screen to Kamara went for 17 yards. Kamara then picked up two yards. Shough then threw it away on second down. A screen to Johnson only picked up a couple of yards, and then Daniel Carlson went wide left.

Brian Robinson Jr. took the first carry for three yards. Brian then went for only a yard. Penix was then sacked on third down while looking downfield. Punt, and Barion Brown got nowhere.

Kendre Miller took it for a couple of yards and appeared to fumble with CJ Henderson recovering, though was ruled down. Kevin Stefanski threw the challenge flag, and after review, Henderson got the fumble recovery.

Bijan took the carry for about three yards, and a holding call on the Saints gave Atlanta another five yards. Chase Young then got his hand up on a play action pass to Bijan which would've been housed. Bijan then took it about three yards on second down, and followed that up with another three yards on third down. The team needed a timeout to sort things out before trying it on fourth down. On fourth down, Penix threw it in the dirt near London, but a holding call on Kool-Aid McKinstry gave Atlanta a fresh set of downs. Bijan then got the blocks and plunged in for a touchdown. 14-0 Falcons.

The return went out past the 30 yard line, but an unnecessary roughness call on Billy Bowman Jr. gave the Saints 15 more yards. Shough then found a wide open Chris Olave, who made it all the way to the 10 yard line. Shough under pressure then hit Bryce Lance for seven yards.

Kamara then got a block, cut inside, and scored a touchdown from three yards out. 14-7 Falcons.

Touchback and the Falcons got it on the 35 yard line. A quick rollout and pass to Kyle Pitts went for nine yards. Brian Robinson Jr. took it for about five yards and a first down. BRJ then took it about seven yards, and followed that up with a two yard delayed plunge. On third down, he worked back inside for three yards and a first down. Bijan went to cut inside, but Jonas Sanker got him for no gain. Penix then found London downfield for a gain of 26. Bijan then picked up a couple, and Penix under pressure got the screen out to Brian Robinson Jr. for six yards. Brian then plunged inside and scored after a nice block by Ryan Neuzxil. 21-7 Falcons.

The kick return was a bit shy of the 30. Miller took it about four yards. A high ball to Vele working against Sydney Brown fell incomplete. Shough then threw a deep ball that was nowhere near Olave. Punt.

On the next play, Penix hung back and found London, who was wide open after McKinstry committed a penalty and fell over, and London got to midfield. Bijan took it ten yards on first down. Bijan then cut it back and evaded tacklers for eight yards. He then picked up a first down. On the next play, Penix got Branch for just a yard. Then Penix hit Pitts over the middle and he picked up a first down. Bijan then cut it in for three yards. Then Penix tried to hit Charlie Woerner, but it was incomplete. Penix then tried Olamide Zaccheaus, but put it out a little too far in front of him and it fell incomplete.

Barion Brown's return went to about the 25 yard line. Shough hit Kamara, who got two yards before Divine Deablo drilled him. Shough then hit Juwan Johnson for 18 yards. A high ball to Johnson went for a couple of yards. Shough then threw it while falling down into the dirt to bring up third down. Shough then hit Olave on a sideline ball for a first down. Xavier Watts then blew into the backfield for a sack. A quick pass to Olave went for six yards. Shough then rolled away from pressure and missed Lance. Punt, but a delay of game backed the Saints up a bit, and the Falcons got it deep in their own territory after the punt.

BJR took it five yards on a first down. A swing pass to London went for a first down. Then we were at the half.

Barion Brown took it past the 30 yard line. Kamara then toted it for four yards. Brandon Dorlus then jumped offsides. Miller then picked up two yards and a first down. Olave then made a sliding catch on a low ball from Shough for a first down. Maason Smith got Miller for a loss of one yard. Shough then threw a swing pass to Kamara, who got seven yards before Henderson got him. Shough then got Johnson, working against Watts, for another first down. Shough tried to connect with Kamara downfield, but Harold Perkins Jr. was smothering him. Kamara then picked up three yards. Olave then reeled in a first down grab on the sideline. On the next play, Shough was way off target but Bowman was called for pass interference, which was a terrible call. Mike Hughes then took Barion Brown on a reverse down for a loss of four yards. The Falcons then picked up a neutral zone infraction. A quick catch by Miller got another five or six yards before Perkins got the tackle. Then Shough had it batted down by Cameron Thomas on third down. The Saints tried the field goal, and got it. 24-10 Saints.

Branch got it back past the 25 yard line. Penix then hung in there and delivered to Jahan Dotson for 20-plus yards, and a defensive offsides was declined. Bijan got eight yards on the next carry. Bijan then took it up the middle for 10 yards. Brian Robinson Jr.'s next handoff was doomed, as he lost two yards. A quick pass to Bijan had nowhere to go after two yards. Penix hung in there with pressure coming and got London for a first down. Bijan then picked up six yards. Brian Robinson then made a nice cut, got some blocking, and scored his second touchdown of the day. 31-10 Falcons.

Barion Brown got a decent return. Shough then slipped multiple sacks and got rid of it, and on the next play saw pressure again and threw it off. Shough then tried the deep ball to Lance and Avieon Terrell got called for pass interference. First down, Shough missed. Shough then threw it to Olave, but they appeared to have a miscommunication. The Shough deep ball to Lance was just a little too far, with the Falcons playing good defense on the play. Unfortunately, Shough got Vele for 18 yards and a first down. Shough then rolled away from pressure and connected, but a holding call on the Saints backed New Orleans up. Shough missed badly to Johnson, but an illegal shift backed the Saints up five more yards. Shough rolled away from pressure to Miller, but Perkins got him for a minimal gain.

title: Disastrous defense sinks Yankees in ALDS Game 2 loss to Rays
description: For the second time in three years, the Yankees had a disastrous defensive game in the postseason and it cost them again, this time in a 5-2 loss to the Rays Monday night in Game 2 of the AL Division Series.
fullText:
For the second time in three years, the Yankees had a disastrous defensive game in the postseason and it cost them again, this time in a 5-2 loss to the Rays Monday night in Game 2 of the AL Division Series.

The Yanks made four errors in the loss, leading to three unearned runs, and they now teeter on the brink of elimination, down two games to none in the best-of-five series. Game 3 is set for Wednesday night at Yankee Stadium.

Two years ago, the Yankee defense collapsed in Game 5 of the World Series against the Dodgers and they were eliminated. But even that game only featured three Yankee errors – in the box score, anyway.

Monday's debacle was only the fifth time the Yankees have made four errors in a single postseason game. The last time was in the 2019 ALCS against the Astros.

The Yankees have scored only twice so far in the series, on two solo home runs by Ben Rice Monday night. No Aaron Judge, who is out with a calf injury, certainly doesn't help.

-- Yankee starter Cam Schlittler was not nearly as brilliant as he's been in his previous postseason outings. He lasted just 4.1 innings and allowed seven hits and four runs (only two earned). He struck out just two and didn't have a strikeout until the fourth inning and got only seven swings-and-misses. He also walked one. His career postseason ERA rose from 0.87 to 1.44.

-- The Yankees defensive implosion started in the very first inning and set a dubious club record for errors in a single postseason frame – three. The Yankees had never had three errors in one October inning and this is the 61st postseason appearance in the Yankees' existence. The Yanks last committed three errors in an inning in any game on Aug. 21, 2025 against the Red Sox. The last time it happened in any postseason game was Game 5 of the 2015 ALDS when the Rangers did it in a loss to the Blue Jays.

-- Ryan McMahon, who has a fine defensive reputation, though he has not had his best season with the glove, made the first miscue when the leadoff hitter, Yandy Díaz, hit a topspin bouncer to him that McMahon muffed. Jonathan Aranda followed with a single and then Junior Caminero hit what could've been a double-play grounder to short. George Lombard Jr. made a not-that-graceful flip to the bag and Jazz Chisholm Jr. grabbed it and threw wildly to first. Díaz scored and Caminero went to second.

Then it seemed like Schlittler had Hicks struck out, but, upon replay review, Austin Wells was called for catcher's interference – his mitt was clearly in the path of Hicks' bat. That was the third error of the inning. They nearly had a fourth – Chisholm fielded Simpson's grounder but threw high to second base, pulling Lombard off the bag. But Lombard got back in time for a force out. Schlittler got a grounder from Victor Mesa to mercifully end the inning. The Yankees only allowed one run, but all the gaffes forced Schlittler to endure some tense moments and extra pitches.

-- The Rays scored four runs in the fifth inning and knocked out Schlittler. They got some weak contact and used their speed to exploit it. Poor Yankee defense helped, too. Aranda started the inning with a single and Caminero followed with a ringing double. With the infield mostly in – Chisholm was further back than the rest of the infielders – Liam Hicks hit a grounder that was slow enough to allow Aranda to score.

Chandler Simpson later hit a soft grounder to short that Lombard couldn't backhand and another run scored. The scoring on that play was changed several times, but it was ultimately scored an infield single. But Lombard then made a throwing error to further prolong the inning and Richie Palacios added a single after an eight-pitch bout with reliever Brent Headrick that scored two more runs.

-- The Yanks went nine up, nine down the first time through their batting order as Rays starter Freddy Peralta looked sharp. But Rice tied the score at 1 with a 372-foot drive over the right-field fence. Rice connected on the fourth of four consecutive changeups from Peralta. Rice also homered in the eighth inning, giving him four home runs in four games this postseason.

-- In the fifth, the Yanks had a big chance with two outs, but could not cash in. Wells lashed a double into the right-field corner that looked a lot like the ball he hit in Game 1 and got thrown out trying to stretch into a triple. He wisely stopped at second this time. McMahon then worked a walk in a tough, seven-pitch at-bat. He was the last batter that Peralta faced. He came out with Rice coming up to the plate.

Rice worked another walk against southpaw Cam Booser, which brought up Cody Bellinger, who was 11th in MLB with a .340 average with runners in scoring position. Bellinger hit a deep fly ball to the warning track in center that held some hope, but it was caught.

-- Peralta, the former Met who got his pitching together in Tampa Bay, lasted 4.2 innings and allowed one run and three hits. He struck out three and walked one. The outing lowered his career postseason ERA from 4.32 to 4.03.
